voice.summary: Sounds like a crew talking over the press at the end of a shift: first person plural, short sentences, ink-under-the-fingernails honesty. Principles are stated as things we do, never as slogans we aspire to.
dos: Use we and our, and name the actual job (sweeping, proofing, folding)
Tell each principle as a small story with a person in it
Keep sentences short enough to read aloud over a noisy press
donts: No corporate values language like synergy or excellence
Never claim a rule without an example of it in practice
Avoid sounding like a manifesto or a recruitment ad

taglines: Printed by people who own the press
Small shop, fair pay, good paper
Ink, paper and a shared broom
boilerplate: Parcel Hill Press is a worker-owned print shop and bindery where every member shares the profits, the decisions and the cleaning rota.
